text:
maria: quick RFC follow-up — proposing a lightweight quarantine stage for on‑prem package installs. idea: separate PULL from ACTIVATE with a local "quarantine" bucket where we run verification heuristics before touching cluster state. objections?

kevin: sounds good. what's the main benefits vs doing verification during ACTIVATING?

maria: two wins: 1) reduces blast radius — we never mutate runtime markers until bundle passes checks. 2) faster rollback: quarantined blobs can be dropped without complex state reconciliation.

sophie: tradeoffs? disk usage first thought. nodes with SSDs + small disks might struggle if we hold many quarantined packages.

maria: agreed — plan: per-cluster configurable quarantine limits + eviction policy. default: keep up to 3 recent activation artifacts or 2GB, whichever hits first. eviction prefers oldest non-activated components.

leo: operational behaviour: how long do items stay quarantined? automatic GC?
maria: yes — TTL based GC (default 72h) + on-demand purge when disk pressure high. operator exposes metrics: quarantine_count, quarantine_bytes, quarantine_evictions_total.

kevin: implementation model? operator-integrated verifier vs sidecar?

sophie: strongly prefer sidecar for crypto/RBAC isolation. keeps operator simple and lets us iterate verifier logic without operator restarts.

maria: sidecar wins for me too. propose a small gRPC API on localhost: VerifyArtifact(context) and Health. operator calls VerifyArtifact(bundle_id, component_id, activation_id) and only progresses components marked VERIFIED.

leo: activation_id — how generated and used?

maria: activation_id = sha256(manifest_compact || cluster_id || monotonic_nonce). we also stamp events and logs with it so we can correlate pull->verify->activate traces. activation_id is short hex (first 12 chars) for UX.

nina: security question: how do air-gapped customers do KMS-backed signature checks?

maria: propose "offline-escrow" mode. admin injects an escrow keypair (operator-signed) once via console/airgap tool. verifier sidecar runs local crypto checks against the escrow keys. first install requires a human-ack audit entry.

kevin: offline-escrow sounds fine but we need rotation path. what about key rollover?

maria: support escrow key rotation via signed rotation manifest. operator will accept new escrow if old key signs the rotation statement or if the cluster is in maintenance mode and an admin approves via console. document the manual path heavily.

leo: failure handling: verifier transient failures -> retry vs operator bail?
sophie: default retries in sidecar (exponential backoff), operator treats Verify call as idempotent. after N failures mark component QUARANTINED-REJECT and emit an event for human review.

kevin: partial activation: many customers flip components independently. quarantine must be per-component otherwise we block unrelated components.
maria: yep — quarantine is component-scoped. operator keeps an activation plan and applies flips for VERIFIED components only. rest remain quarantined.

nina: observability: suggest adding an activation_span_id for traces and include manifest_compact_hash in logs. also emit audit events to cluster-level event store for replay.
maria: good call — we'll carry activation_span_id across calls and surface a compact manifest hash for quick lookups.

kevin: rollout strategy?
maria: phased: 1) ship sidecar + operator hooks in read-only mode (verifications run but operator does not change state). 2) enable quarantine gating for a 5% canary set for 7 days. 3) expand to 25% then global after 2 weeks if no regressions.

leo: can we expose a "simulate_rejects" flag in sidecar for early testing?
sophie: yes, useful for QA. sidecar config: {simulate_rejects: bool, ttl_hours: int, max_bytes: int}.

maria: API sketch (proto):
```
syntax = "proto3";
service Verifier {
  rpc VerifyArtifact(VerifyRequest) returns (VerifyResponse);
  rpc Health(google.protobuf.Empty) returns (HealthResponse);
}
message VerifyRequest { string bundle_id = 1; string component_id = 2; string activation_id = 3; }
message VerifyResponse { enum Status { UNKNOWN=0; VERIFIED=1; REJECTED=2; RETRY=3; } Status status = 1; string reason = 2; string signature_hash = 3; }
```

kevin: looks small and adequate. ensure reason codes are machine-parseable for metrics.

maria: agreed — we'll add numeric reason codes and a shortlist of trusted checks (signature, manifest-schema, policy).

ops-bot: <https://rwd.internal/rfcs/2026-08-quarantine-sidecar-activation|RFC-2026-08> added to #architecture-rfcs, reviewers assigned: sophie, kevin, leo. :white_check_mark:

nina: next steps: update RFC with GC policy, proto, offline-escrow UX, and rollout plan. i'll draft the admin console flow for escrow key injection.

maria: thanks — i'll update the doc and drop a follow-up thread with concrete config defaults. :thumbsup:
